title: 1CA2 Carbonic anhydrase II curated conservation teaching set
classification: straightforward single-protein reference; human carbonic anhydrase II with zinc cofactor
teachingQuestion: Which CA II residues are conserved across vertebrate orthologs, and how do zinc binding and proton transfer constrain the active site?

alignment.gapTreatment: Gap columns are included in display; amino-acid conservation scoring excludes gaps from residue-frequency counts.

studentContext.whatIsCompared: Vertebrate carbonic anhydrase II orthologs, not mixed beta/gamma carbonic anhydrases or distant alpha-CA paralogs.
studentContext.whySelected: Sequences are full-length CA II-like records with compatible 260-aa architecture and high reference coverage.
studentContext.whatConservationMeans: Similarity within this CA II ortholog set; conserved positions can suggest structural or catalytic constraints but need biochemical evidence for functional claims.
studentContext.whatToNotice: Zinc ligands, His64 proton-transfer context, and residues shaping the active-site pocket.
limitations: The set emphasizes CA II orthologs; it is not a broad carbonic-anhydrase-family comparison.
Some non-mammalian CA II annotations are less experimentally characterized than human/mammalian records.
